15e6c33152538012: Karl Schmidt was born in 1884 in Rottluff (now Chemnitz). He is co-founder of the artist group Brücke and an important representative of Expressionism in Germany. After many years of initiatives and preliminary planning, the city of Chemnitz decided to transform the former home of Karl Schmidt-Rottluff at Limbacher Straße 382 into an artists' house. Together with the neighbouring mill, the house is being expanded into another hotspot of Expressionism in Chemnitz.
169975601f4c4dd8: How do images make social and political realities tangible? What knowledge do they impart? And how are they themselves entangled in the production of reality? The exhibition "It's not about nothing" presents cinematic and photographic works that question the visible through documentary means. They take us to different places: a Nazi fortress in the south of France or a tomato plantation in Puglia, a prefabricated housing estate in Halle or the interior of the Statue of Liberty in New York, a publishing house in Sarajevo or a square in Bratislava. In two episodes, the exhibition shows works from the GfZK collection, invited artistic positions and diploma presentations. The examination of the documentary will be expanded between July and October to include works that deal with image archives, among other things.
2ac2d42fe2198826: Experience Frida Kahlo as close and intense as never before. Viva Frida Kahlo is a multimedia 360°exhibition that transforms the art, life and emotions of the world-famous artist into an impressive digital experience. Immerse yourself in the colorful world of Mexico and travel to Casa Azul in Coyoacán - the place where Frida Kahlo found her artistic voice after a serious accident. High-resolution projections, room-filling images, and an atmospheric soundscape bring the 1920s through 1940s to life, opening a new doorway to her powerful paintings and iconic self-portraits. Bright colours, strong symbols and Frida Kahlo's unmistakable visual language unfold as an emotional overall experience that touches, inspires and has a long lasting effect.
59740e806fa3c5e5: In February 2016, Yadegar Asisi made her first trip to Antarctica - a region known for its extreme living conditions as well as its overwhelming beauty and monumental silence. Exactly ten years later, on 24 January, his new panorama exhibition ANTARCTICA opened at the Panometer Leipzig. The 32-metre-high circular image takes visitors to one of the most hostile and fascinating regions on earth - where water and ice meet in the Antarctic coastal landscape. Huge ice formations and glaciers tower above the water's surface in the 360°panorama, while a fragile and astonishingly diverse ecosystem with numerous marine animals reveals itself underneath. The visual experience is intensified in the panoramic image with a 15-minute day and night simulation. Light changes, auroras, matching background noises and music bring the scenery to life and give you the feeling of immersing yourself up close in this overwhelming landscape. The giant picture is complemented by an accompanying exhibition with photographs, exhibits and drawings. They illuminate climate, geology and wildlife as well as Yadegar Asisi's personal, artistic access to this unique continent.
59c6a1ebb0cd498e: With Der Lauf (AT), the Kunstverein 47m Contemporary presents the first solo exhibition of the Kurdish artist Leyla Yenirce in East Germany. Yenirce's multimedia work revolves around the confrontation with women in resistance, collective memory and political complicity in the context of Kurdish-feminist freedom struggles. The exhibition shows sound and video works, with the focus on a multi-channel video work produced especially for the exhibition, which brings Yenirce's own body into dialogue with local feminist stories of Leipzig.

605a42b9be887b84: The collection of the Leipziger Hof occupies a special place among the private collections of German art of the 20th century, as it contains numerous main works of painting of the "Leipziger Schule". In almost complete unity, the collection presents in particular the painting of the short, eruptive phase of young German history, the Reunification period - both art-historically and as a contemporary historical document. The founder of the hotel and retired Munich physics professor Dr. Klaus Eberhard compiled the more than 350 works in the years from 1990 to the present in close cooperation with the city's museums and with Leipzig art historians. Despite being hung in a hotel, the intimate, private character of the collection has been preserved. Probably also because Eberhard never acquired "en bloc" and only aesthetic aspects and the quality of the exhibits - often reassured by the judgment of friendly art historians - were and are the main features of the collection. Works by more than 70 Leipzig artists are shown - the spectrum ranges from the "fathers" of the Leipzig School such as Heisig, Mattheuer, Mayer-Foreyt and Tübke to Gille, Rink, Ebersbach, Minkewitz and Müller-Simon to the young, globally celebrated artists of the "New Leipzig School" such as Weischer, Triegel, Loy and others. The collection is constantly being supplemented.

8fac7efae7635a92: Cornelia Aichinger works very illustratively. Her colourful paper works refer to the book illustration of the Romantic period. df95d4483175f7b8: Ulf Rickmann creates an idiosyncratic natural cosmos in painting, drawing & graphics: populated by imaginary insects and hybrid plants, his pictorial worlds seem familiar and alien. Inspired by studies of nature, he condenses forms into whimsical, often mystical-looking compositions that oscillate between observation and invention.
edbc0e0964be9384: The exhibition Knots of the Time brings together works by three artists from Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Ukraine/Switzerland. They deal with cultural influences: the faiths into which they were born, the cities in which they grew up, their parents' professions. Moments from the past weave them into new, imaginative narratives that revolve around queer identity or family relationships, for example. They work artistically with a variety of materials and media such as textiles, installation and performance. "The sensations, images and allegories in dreams fascinate: As knots of time, dreams connect the past, present and future. They contain clues and warnings, inspiration and discoveries, answers and questions for yourself and the world." Bjeshkë Guri and Ilirjana Blakaj in: The Catalogue of Dreams, a research book on dream interpretation in various regions of Kosovo.
eeaaec4dfc5f2e8a: Bright flowers, finely drawn landscapes, portraits with a deep view - Margarethe Freudenberg (1876 - 1939) created well over a hundred watercolours, drawings and oil paintings in just seven years. Born in Berlin as a contemporary of Paula Modersohn-Becker, she received drawing lessons in her hometown from the painters Franz Skarbina and Ludwig Dettmann. In 1899 she became engaged, married and had six children in the following years. She gave up painting. Only after her death did her children find the drawings and watercolors hidden in an attic. Today, many works have been preserved or rediscovered and have been brought to light in two exhibitions. For the first time, the images of great gift and creative power could be seen in public. For the 150th Birthday of Margarethe Freudenberg, this anniversary exhibition presents a selection of the versatile work and pays tribute to an unknown artist. The exhibition will be inaugurated on its birthday, July 31, in the presence of the descendants.
